x.text:
Fed governor Lisa Cook explains her October dissent for the first time.

Her two reasons: policy is too easy (“not curtailing the AI buildout,” and stock gains are propping up spending) with "no clear signs of disinflation in train." And waiting risks falling behind the curve, which would mean “additional and larger rate increases” later. 

"My vote reflected the urgency I feel to tackle inflation."

"In a different environment, the Committee could afford to be patient, but I continue to believe that in this economic climate we do not have that luxury."

According to Luxor’s Hashrate Index, the drop was driven primarily by surging electricity prices in West Texas rather than falling BTC prices. A sharp decline in wind generation and transmission constraints pushed daily average power prices to $64–$122/MWh from November 7 to 11, above the roughly $54/MWh average breakeven level for miners operating at 25 J/TH.
